content.comment_body: Hello, I'm new to [product_name], so I might be overlooking something basic. Previously, I raised this question in another thread but thought it might be better to start a new topic. I'm attempting to create a User Defined Function (UDF) because my circuit diagram is running out of space. After creating and saving the UDF, I added it to the UDF library, but it's greyed out and can't be used in the circuit diagram—it appears usable only when you're building another UDF (see the attached image). I suspect I'm missing a simple step and would appreciate any guidance.

Hi, you're saying you're running out of space in your circuit diagram. Are you aware you can add multiple pages? There's a button near the highlighter tool: a white page with numbered tabs. Regarding the UDF library being greyed out, check if your [product_name] hardware selection in the UDT matches your project's hardware configuration. If your UDT uses one hardware version and your project another, compatibility issues may arise. The image shows the UDT containing a specific hardware variant.
Thanks for your advice—I didn’t know multiple sheets could be used or that the UDF controller type could be changed. Everything's working now!

I'm experiencing a similar issue. I created a UDF, and when using the UDF creator, the UDF tab lets me access my own functions. But when working on an FBD, the UDF library with my custom functions isn’t visible at all. I’m using version [version_no].

The software points to a specific location on your disk for these UDFs. If you set the software to reference where your UDFs are stored, it will make them accessible again. It would be much more convenient if there were a way for the software to look for UDFs in a folder relative to the project location.

For me, the issue was a mismatch between the hardware selected in the main project and the hardware for the UDF project. My main project used one version, while the UDF project had another. To fix this: go to Tools > Select Hardware and choose the correct type.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report challenges using User Defined Functions (UDFs) within circuit diagrams due to issues like unavailable or inactive UDFs, often caused by mismatched hardware settings between projects and UDF configurations and non-intuitive library management. New users also struggle with features such as adding multiple pages to circuit diagrams.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect the ability to easily create, save, and reuse UDFs in circuit diagrams without technical difficulties. They look for straightforward compatibility across hardware versions and intuitive, seamless access to UDF libraries.
